messages.subject: mean-variance relationship and model bulding in stam
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about model building if mean variance relationship is know.  I have used quite simple approach - sorted all outputs y, placed them into bins of equal size, and calculated mean and variance for each bin.  The final result looks like quadratic function f (mu) - attached.  I have tried different bin sizes - shape is the same.  I saw this technique somewhere on the internet (don't recall where).  Is such model going to be valid/make sense:
y ~ normal (mu, f(mu))? where mu=x*beta, x are inputs, beta is the vector of parameters to estimate.  Maybe I should try other link functions in addition to identity link?

I appreciate any comments.

Thank you,
Linas

The final result looks like quadratic function f (mu) - attached. I have tried different bin sizes - shape is the same. I saw this technique somewhere on the internet (don't recall where). Is such model going to be valid/make sense:
> y ~ normal (mu, f(mu))? where mu=x*beta, x are inputs, beta is the vector of parameters to estimate. Maybe I should try other link functions in addition to identity link?

I didn't see your f(mu), but based on the plot, with is labeled
as log(mean) vs. log(var), I'm guessing it's:

f(mu) = sqrt(exp(log(mu)^2))

perhaps with some scaling of inputs and outputs.

You can do that as long as mu > 0. Try it and see how it fits the
data.

- Bob
